  "text": "Martin found his father in the shed, sorting screws into a biscuit tin.

“The taxi’s booked for ten,” Martin said.

“I know what time it is.”

His father held a screw against the light, then dropped it into a compartment made from folded cardboard.

“Do you need that?”

“Not today.”

Martin stood beside the lawnmower. There was scarcely room for his feet. On the bench, a mug held three paintbrushes with their bristles hardened into points.

“They said you can take a small bag.”

“It’s by the door.”

“I saw.”

“Then why are you asking?”

Outside, rain ticked against the water butt. Martin picked up a wooden handle with no tool attached.

“That’s for the file,” his father said.

“Where’s the file?”

“Missing.”

Martin put the handle down.

His father tried to close the tin, but a long screw lay across the rim. He moved it. The lid still wouldn’t sit properly.

“Here,” Martin said.

“I’ve got it.”

They waited while a car passed along the lane. His father pressed each corner of the lid with the heel of his hand.

“Your mother used to keep the spare keys in this.”

“I remember.”

“No, that was the round one. With the dog.”

Martin checked his phone without waking the screen.

“Will you lock up?” his father asked.

“Of course.”

“The shed as well.”

“Yes.”

His father reached behind the paintbrushes and brought out a key on a loop of string. He held it for a moment before passing it over.

“The lock sticks. Lift the door a bit.”

Martin put the key in his pocket.

“You can show me,” he said."
